**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/02/18 (Sat) 17:02
- [USER] User inquired about tax deductions on salary and their relation to advance tax.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Income tax deductions on salary are not considered "advance tax."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Advance tax is a payment of tax made before the final determination of the tax liability for a given tax year.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Income tax deductions on salary are reductions in the amount of salary that is subject to income tax.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Taxpayers may claim deductions to lower their tax liability.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common examples of deductions that may be claimed on salary income include deductions for charitable donations, mortgage interest, and contributions to retirement savings plans.
